summary: Moises Benzaquen Rengifo Airport (YMS) serves the riverside city of Yurimaguas in Peru's Loreto region, acting as a vital aerial gateway to the central Amazon rainforest. Named after a local aviation pioneer, the airport connects this remote jungle community with Lima and other regional hubs, supporting both passenger travel and cargo operations essential to the area's economy. Its location near the confluence of the Paranapura and Huallaga rivers makes it a key starting point for ecotourism and river expeditions into the Amazon basin.
faqs:
Q: How far is Moises Benzaquen Rengifo Airport from Yurimaguas city center?
A: The airport is located just a few kilometers from downtown Yurimaguas, with typical transfer times of around 15-20 minutes depending on traffic and river crossings.

Q: What is the airport commonly used for?
A: It primarily serves domestic flights connecting Yurimaguas to Lima and other Peruvian cities, and acts as an access point for tourists heading into the Amazon rainforest and nearby river systems.

Q: Are there regular commercial flights to Lima from this airport?
A: Yes, there are scheduled domestic flights operating between Yurimaguas and Lima, though schedules can vary by season and demand.

Q: Can I travel onward to the Amazon jungle from this airport?
A: Absolutely. Many travelers use the airport as a jumping-off point for guided tours, river cruises, and expeditions into the surrounding rainforest and protected areas.
transport_tips: Mototaxis are the most common and affordable way to reach the airport from central Yurimaguas, often costing just a few soles for the short trip. Shared vans and small minibuses also operate along main routes and can be flagged down near the terminal. Given the tropical climate and occasional heavy rains, it's wise to allow extra travel time, especially during the wet season when roads may flood.
local_tip: Pack insect repellent and a light rain jacket in your carry-on—even short waits at this jungle airport can expose you to mosquitoes and sudden downpours typical of the Amazonian climate.
